topIssues.title: op/kona-node lite: follow both local_safe and safe heads from source
topIssues.author: geoknee
topIssues.body:
An op-node configured for lite mode (following a source instead of doing derivation itself) will currently set the local_safe head of the upstream safe head.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/80804af288d016d28bf26e3b14e58679bb070d87/op-node/rollup/driver/driver.go#L550

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/80804af288d016d28bf26e3b14e58679bb070d87/op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go#L1221-L1222

This can be problematic for interop, where sequencers run as lite CLs. In that setup, the local safe of the sequencer will lag the _actual_ local safe, since the unqualified `safe` label is delayed until interop verification finishes. This confuses the op-batcher, if it connects to the sequencer, since it expects local safe head progression after posting batch txs. It can erroneously enter a recovery mode where it loads more blocks than it should. 

We should update the engine controller to track both heads so the sync status of a lite CL lines up with that of a supernode.

topIssues.title: op-reth v1.11.0 tls issue
topIssues.author: bhaveshtank
topIssues.body:
**Bug Description**

The `op-reth` binary from the OP Labs Docker image (`us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-reth:v1.11.0`) fails to connect to the flashblocks WebSocket endpoint with the error `"URL error: TLS support not compiled in"`. 

**Steps to Reproduce**

1. Pull the OP Labs op-reth image: `docker pull us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-reth:v1.11.0`
2. Run op-reth with flashblocks enabled using `--flashblocks-url wss://<flashblocks-endpoint>/ws` on Optimism Mainnet
3. Observe the repeating WARN log every 5 seconds: `Error receiving flashblock err=URL error: TLS support not compiled in`

**Expected behavior**

op-reth should successfully establish a WSS connection to the flashblocks endpoint and receive flashblock data for building pending state.

**Environment Information:**

- Operating System: Linux (Docker)
- Docker Image: `us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-reth:v1.11.0`
- Package Version: op-reth v1.11.0
- Chain: Optimism Mainnet

**Configurations:**

```
--flashblocks-url wss://<flashblocks-endpoint>/ws
```

**Logs:**

```
2026-02-26T13:22:43.867284Z  WARN Error receiving flashblock err=URL error: TLS support not compiled in retry_period=5
2026-02-26T13:22:48.881971Z  WARN Error receiving flashblock err=URL error: TLS support not compiled in retry_period=5
2026-02-26T13:22:53.890658Z  WARN Error receiving flashblock err=URL error: TLS support not compiled in retry_period=5

```

topPRs.title: feat(contracts-bedrock): add compliance module for cross-chain transaction screening
topPRs.author: tynes
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Design doc: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/367

- Adds an optional compliance screening layer for cross-chain transactions on `OptimismPortal2` (L1 deposits) and `L2ToL1MessagePasser` (L2 withdrawals)
- Introduces `Compliance` abstract contract with configurable rules, pending/approved/rejected status tracking, and ETH escrow for flagged transactions
- Concrete `L1Compliance` and `L2Compliance` implementations override `_executeApproved` to call the correct bridge
- Adds `approved()` and `donateETH()` callbacks on `OptimismPortal2` and `L2ToL1MessagePasser` for compliance settlement
- Updates `ICompliance`, `IL2ToL1MessagePasserCGT`, and `IOptimismPortal2` interfaces
- Bumps `OPContractsManager` to 6.0.4 and `OPContractsManagerV2` to 7.0.9
- Comprehensive test coverage across unit, integration, and end-to-end tests

topPRs.title: feat: Implement L2 Dev Flags
topPRs.author: 0xiamflux
topPRs.body:
## Overview
                                                                                                                                                       
  Added L2DevFeatureFlags predeploy at 0x420...002d that stores a per-chain dev feature bitmap, enabling L2CM to gate predeploy upgrades behind feature flags.

## Changes:
  - New L2DevFeatureFlags — stores bitmap in a custom storage slot.
  - Interop gating: 7 interop predeploys wrapped in if (_isDevFeatureEnabled(DevFeatures.OPTIMISM_PORTAL_INTEROP)) — when disabled, proxies are not upgraded.
  - L2CM upgrades the predeploy: L2CM now includes L2DevFeatureFlags in its upgrade flow.  
  - Genesis: `L2Genesis.setL2DevFeatureFlags()` deploys the impl and sets the bitmap at genesis via `DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT`.

topPRs.title: supernode: store full OutputV0 in denylist
topPRs.author: axelKingsley
topPRs.body:
# Tool Use Notice
Entirely Generated. This PR just changes one data type for another (superset) data type, and corrects the related integrations.

# What
Update the DenyList to store the complete eth.OutputV0 structure instead of just the block hash. This enables retrieval of the StateRoot and MessagePasserStorageRoot for invalidated blocks, as well as the calculation of the Output Root of any invalidated blocks we no longer have access to.

Changes:
- DenyList.Add() now accepts *eth.OutputV0 parameter
- Added DenyList.GetOutput() to retrieve full OutputV0 for denied blocks
- Storage format: 96 bytes per entry (hash + StateRoot + MsgPasserRoot)
- ChainContainer.InvalidateBlock() now requires *eth.OutputV0
- Added ChainContainer.OutputV0AtL2BlockNumber() to fetch full output
- Interop activity fetches OutputV0 before invalidating blocks
- Updated all mock implementations and tests

topPRs.title: fix(contracts-bedrock): make CI reliable
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Fixes `VerifyOPCM_Failed()` CI failures caused by `vm.getCode("ProxyAdmin")` non-deterministically resolving to the `dispute` compiler profile's artifact (optimized with 5000 runs) instead of the default profile's artifact (999999 runs).

### Root cause

When `additional_compiler_profiles` is configured in `foundry.toml`, `vm.getCode(name)` can resolve to any matching artifact. For contracts compiled under both `default` and `dispute` profiles (e.g., `ProxyAdmin`), the resolved artifact is non-deterministic, causing bytecode mismatches in `VerifyOPCM` assertions.

### Fix

1. **`DeployUtils.getCode()`** — New wrapper that constructs the explicit artifact path (`forge-artifacts/<Name>.sol/<Name>.json`) to always resolve the default profile. Wrapped in `try/catch` so the Go script host in `op-chain-ops` (which doesn't support artifact paths but has no profile ambiguity) gracefully falls back to `vm.getCode(_name)`. Callers passing qualified identifiers (`:` or `/`) are passed through as-is.

2. **Migration** — 12 `vm.getCode()` call sites across 4 files migrated to `DeployUtils.getCode()`.

3. **Semgrep rule** — Bans direct `vm.getCode(...)` usage outside `DeployUtils.sol` to prevent regressions.

4. **L1ChugSplashProxy gas test** — Under `cicoverage`, the fix changes which artifact is loaded (from accidentally-optimized dispute artifact to correctly-unoptimized default). The larger bytecode shifts gas dynamics in the OOG test. Uses generic `vm.expectRevert()` for unoptimized profiles (the test still verifies the revert occurs, just without matching the specific error string).

### No Go changes

The `try/catch` fallback eliminates the need for any `op-chain-ops` modifications.

## Files changed (vs develop)

| File | What changes |
|------|-------------|
| `packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/libraries/DeployUtils.sol` | Add `getCode()` with try/catch fallback; use in `create1`, `create2`, `createDeterministic` |
| `packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/deploy/ChainAssertions.sol` | 5x `vm.getCode` → `DeployUtils.getCode` |
| `packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/deploy/DeployImplementations.s.sol` | 5x `vm.getCode` → `DeployUtils.getCode` |
| `packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/L2Genesis.s.sol` | 1x `vm.getCode` → `DeployUtils.getCode` |
| `packages/contracts-bedrock/test/L2/FeeSplitter.t.sol` | 1x `vm.getCode` → `DeployUtils.getCode` |
| `packages/contracts-bedrock/test/legacy/L1ChugSplashProxy.t.sol` | Add `cicoverage` condition + generic `vm.expectRevert()` for unoptimized |
| `.semgrep/rules/sol-rules.yaml` | Ban `vm.getCode(...)` outside DeployUtils.sol |
| `.semgrep/tests/sol-rules.t.sol` | Test cases for the semgrep rule |

topPRs.title: test(contracts): convert GovernanceToken tests to fuzz tests
topPRs.author: devin-ai-integration
topPRs.body:
# test(contracts): convert GovernanceToken tests to fuzz tests

## Summary

Converts all 9 hardcoded-value tests in `GovernanceToken.t.sol` to fuzz tests, broadening input coverage without adding or removing any test functions.

**Mint_Test:**
- `testFuzz_mint_fromOwner_succeeds` — fuzzes recipient address and mint amount
- `testFuzz_mint_fromNotOwner_reverts` — fuzzes caller address for access control

**Uncategorized_Test (inherited ERC20 functions):**
- `burn`, `burnFrom`, `transfer`, `transferFrom` — fuzz both mint and operation amounts
- `approve` — fuzzes allowance amount (removed unnecessary mint, since approval doesn't require balance)
- `increaseAllowance` / `decreaseAllowance` — fuzz initial allowance and delta

**Bounds rationale:**
- Mint amounts bounded to `type(uint224).max` because `ERC20Votes` uses `uint224` for vote checkpoints; larger values revert with `"ERC20Votes: total supply risks overflowing votes"`
- `increaseAllowance` parameters bounded to `type(uint128).max` each to prevent overflow when summing

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Verify the `uint224` upper bound on mint amounts matches the `ERC20Votes` safe ceiling — a value above this should revert, so the bound is correct
- [ ] Confirm the `uint128` bounds in `testFuzz_increaseAllowance_anyAmount_succeeds` are sufficient to prevent arithmetic overflow while still providing meaningful fuzz range
- [ ] Spot-check that removing the `mint` call from the `approve` test doesn't lose coverage (ERC20 `approve` has no balance requirement)

### Notes
- All 10 tests pass locally (1 constructor + 2 mint + 7 uncategorized)
- `forge fmt` and semgrep clean; `pre-pr` failure is from a pre-existing `semver-lock-no-build` issue (missing source files unrelated to this change)
- No new test functions added; no tests removed — strictly a fuzz conversion
